evidence.statement: The items consistently reflect the source distinctions: recognition converts speech to text, synthesis converts text to audio, MFCCs summarize speech features, and domain adaptation supports specialized terminology.
Each item provides a determinable answer, with explicit correct answers or accepted-answer sets; the arrangement items use word banks that support one intended sentence.
Multiple-choice distractors represent nearby but incorrect concepts, such as confusing MFCC preparation with audio capture or confusing decoding settings with domain adaptation.

Wrong-choice labels and rationales diagnose realistic misconceptions, including speech-only design, output-quality confusion, recognition-versus-synthesis confusion, and real-time-versus-batch latency confusion.

The sequence moves from capability identification and common use cases into MFCCs, acoustic modeling, language modeling, implementation considerations, and combined applications, with applying-level scenarios appearing throughout.
The session uses true/false, arrange-sentence, fill-blank, single-choice, and multi-choice mechanics across the ordered sequence, avoiding long uninterrupted runs of one mechanic.
Prompt stems vary among direct claims, completion prompts, reconstruction instructions, and contextual scenarios such as clinical, vehicle, language-learning, and customer-service settings.
Application scenarios closely match source examples, including healthcare documentation, call routing, language learning, vehicle commands, accessibility, and live voice assistants.
Explanations generally identify the governing concept and clarify the next step, for example distinguishing capture from MFCC preparation and recognition from synthesis.
The artifact is an introductory checkpoint: foundational recall items are mixed with moderate applying scenarios, while deeper technical concepts remain bounded to source-described relationships.
Recognition/speech-to-text, synthesis/text-to-speech, MFCC, phoneme, language model, domain adaptation, and latency are used consistently with the source.

The exact sequence is source-faithful, varied, scenario-grounded, and supported by corrective explanations; its main limitation is that some technical pipeline and planning concepts are interleaved rather than grouped into a maximally smooth progression.

result.concise_summary: The session is a strong, source-faithful introductory checkpoint with clear answers, plausible misconception-based distractors, varied mechanics, and useful feedback. No critical defect or threshold-failing actionable gap is evident; confidence is modestly reduced because no approved exemplars were supplied.
